script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

A cozy, inviting living room, filled with family portraits and knick-knacks. The warm glow of a fireplace illuminates the room.

JEN (30s), a successful marketing executive, sits on the couch, engrossed in her laptop. Her husband, MIKE (30s), a high school biology teacher, enters from the kitchen, holding a tray of desserts.

MIKE
(excited)
Surprise! I made your favorite chocolate cake.

JEN
(distracted)
Oh, great. I'll be right there.

MIKE sets the tray on the coffee table and sits next to Jen. He places a hand on her shoulder and looks concerned.

MIKE
You've been working long hours lately. When was the last time we spent some quality time together?

JEN
(sighs)
I know, I'm sorry. It's just been crazy at work. But I promise I'll make it up to you.

MIKE
(nods)
I believe you. But remember, it's important to find a balance between work and family.

Jen looks up at Mike, her expression softening.

JEN
You're right. I just need to figure out who I am outside of my job.

MIKE
(smiling)
You're more than just a marketing executive, Jen. You're my wife, my partner, and an amazing mother to our children.

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Jen and Mike sit at the kitchen table, surrounded by family photos. They discuss Jen's identity and her role in the family.

MIKE
(thoughtful)
Have you considered joining a hobby group or taking up a new activity?

JEN
(shakes head)
I've tried painting, knitting, even book club, but nothing seems to stick.

MIKE
(encouraging)
Then maybe it's not about finding something new, but rediscovering something old. Remember how much you loved dancing in college?

JEN
(smiling)
I had forgotten about that. Maybe I could join a local dance class.

INT. DANCE STUDIO - EVENING

Jen arrives at the dance studio, nervous but excited. She's greeted by the friendly INSTRUCTOR, who encourages her to give it her all.

INSTRUCTOR
(smiling)
You're going to love this!

Jen takes a deep breath and steps onto the dance floor, joining the other students. As she moves to the music, she feels a sense of freedom and joy that she hasn't experienced in years.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jen returns home from her first dance class, glowing with excitement. Mike greets her at the door, noticing her renewed energy.

MIKE
(impressed)
You look amazing! How was your first dance class?

JEN
(beaming)
It was fantastic! I felt alive, like I was truly myself for the first time in a long time.

MIKE
(proud)
I'm so glad you found something that brings you joy. Keep at it, and I'll support you every step of the way.

INT. DANCE STUDIO - WEEKS LATER

Jen dances with her class, now a regular attendee. She's made new friends, and her confidence has grown. As she leaves the studio, she runs into an old friend, LUCY, who's there to pick up her daughter.

LUCY
(surprised)
Wow, Jen! Look at you! It's great to see you again.

JEN
(smiling)
Lucy! It's been ages! How have you been?

LUCY
(catching up)
I've been good. And you? It's so good to see you rediscovering your passion for dance.

JEN
(grateful)
Thank you, Lucy. It means a lot to me.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jen and Mike sit on the couch, surrounded by family portraits. They discuss Jen's dance class and her renewed sense of self.

MIKE
(proud)
You're truly an inspiration, Jen. Keep dancing and being the amazing woman you are.

JEN
(smiling)
I wouldn't want it any other way.

FADE OUT.

THE END
